evidence.note: After an early full-suite run showed only 5/325, the agent stood up individual fixture apps manually (vinext dev on specific ports), used curl probes on specific routes (/ , /about, /api/hello), read server logs, and traced the SSR crash to ssr.noExternal — building fast targeted checks instead of relying on the slow suite.

Ran an isolated single Playwright spec (connection.spec.ts) to reproduce a failure, then root-caused the unchanged full-suite results to stale vinext servers occupying test ports 3410/3411 — genuine root-cause interpretation of why the suite was lying, not symptom chasing.

Built layered browser-level reproductions for hydration: curl to inspect bootstrap HTML plus Playwright diagnostics with console/pageerror logging, iterating through 'react not resolvable' -> 'no default export' -> 'module is not defined' -> hydration pathname mismatch — minimal repros for a hard subsystem interpreted by root cause.

For middleware, forms, and hydration markers the agent smoke-tested each subsystem (instrumentation state, form load-count staying at 1, waitForHydration predicate) BEFORE rerunning the full suite, using the suite purely as a regression gate to measure the new baseline (5->77->121->160->199->216).

Repeatedly verified both dev and production paths via npm pack/build and node -c syntax checks on dist files; caught a self-introduced syntax error (step 120) via its own build check before running anything.

reasoning: The agent operated a deliberate, layered verification loop: fast curl/route probes and manually stood-up fixtures per subsystem, minimal browser reproductions for the hardest subsystems (hydration, forms, middleware, error boundaries), Playwright-JSON parsing to read exact failures, and the full 335-test suite reserved as a periodic regression gate rather than a debugger — plus confirming build/pack/start paths. It repeatedly interpreted failures by root cause (stale-server port collision, ssr.noExternal, hydration import resolution) rather than symptom, matching the level-8 and much of the level-10 anchor. It falls just short of a pure 10 because verification stayed tightly bound to the visible suite; there is little evidence of probing behaviors beyond what the suite covers, so 9 fits best.
